To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a fourfold classification of identity statuses was developed and (2) the four statuses were found to have different implications for the individual's ability to cope with the stress of the concept attainment task and to set realistic goals.

(1) the four ego identity statuses are distinct, reliable, and valid, (2) the identity diffusion status is characterized by low self esteem and high authoritarianism and (3) ego identity achievement is associated with good performance on a concept attainment task.

(a) ego identity status can be reliably determined by means of an interview; (b) ego identity status is a significant determinant of performance in a stressful concept attainment situation and of goal setting patterns; (c) the status characterized by commitment to parental values is associated with authoritarianism; and (d) the status characterizedby commitment to parental values and the status of identity diffusion are associated with a high vulnerability to self esteem loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable and valid measure of ego identity.

the validation of the identity statuses and the exploration of the relationship between ego identity and the following variables: performance on a stressful conceptattainment task, authoritarianism, goal setting, and vulnerability to change in self esteem.
the development of a reliable, valid method for measuring ego identity and with the exploration of ego identity as a variable in the study of personality and adjustment.

there are no conclusive studies.
there is a need for further research on the ego identity status concept.
ego identity status is a valid and reliable measure of the degree to which the individual has achieved a sense of continuity within himself in the face of adult demands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ego identity status measure was a reliable, valid, and useful instrument for the assessment of the identity crisis.
identity diffusion, the absence of crisis and commitment, was associated with a lack of ego strength.
identity status is a reliable, valid, and meaningful construct which is related to a number of other important psychological variables.
